D009-D001_h001.question:
"Lately, it's just been a rollercoaster, doctor. For about a month now, I've been running on fumes, literally. Sleep? Who needs it? I feel like I could conquer the world, full of ideas for the business, just *driven* to get things done. But then I get this restless energy; I can't sit still, find myself pacing the office, or even at home, just needing to *do* something, anything. My wife says I don't stop talking, just keep going and going, but it feels like there's so much to say, so many thoughts buzzing. Sometimes I feel on top of the world, then suddenly I'm snapping at people, getting irritable over nothing.

But that's just the last month. Before that, for about a year, it's been... heavy. A constant gloom that just won't lift. Even when I close a big deal, or things are going great with the company, it just doesn't register. It's like, 'So what?' My brain just feels tired all the time, thinking is such an effort. And honestly, there are days I just think, 'I can't do this anymore. I just want it all to stop.' No real plans, just that feeling, you know? It's really started to affect everything, my work, my marriage... I just feel stuck."
D009-D001_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D009-D001_h001.answer: B & C. Bipolar II Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D009-D001_h002.question:

Most days, I can barely drag myself out of bed, and the thought of facing another interpreting gig, even one I used to love, just leaves me cold. Nothing brings me joy anymore; everything feels flat and gray. Even small things, like walking up a flight of stairs, leave me absolutely drained, like I’ve run a marathon. There was one time, a few months ago, when things got so bad I just couldn't see a way out. I… I tried to end it all, just to make the pain stop.

Before all this gloom settled in, though, there was a period, maybe a month or so back, where I felt completely different. I was on fire! I’d be up all night, buzzing with ideas, translating articles just for fun, and feeling like I only needed an hour or two of sleep to conquer the world. I’d start multiple projects, feeling unstoppable, chattering away to anyone who’d listen, sometimes to the point where I think I was overwhelming them. But then, if someone interrupted my flow or questioned me, I'd get so incredibly annoyed, snappy even. I remember pacing endlessly while on the phone, just needing to move, feeling this restless energy under my skin. It was intense, and I got so much done, but it also felt a little… out of control. Now, though, it’s just back to this heavy sadness, and I don't know why.

A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

"It's just… I’m so tired all the time now, doctor. For over a year, it feels like I’m moving through mud. Simple things, like picking up the dustpan, take all my effort. And honestly, I just don’t care anymore. My kids tell me I did a great job with their upbringing, and I just… feel nothing. It’s like my feelings are all numb and faraway. This slowness has really affected my work; I can’t clean houses like I used to.

But then there are other times, and those lasted about three months recently, where it’s the complete opposite. I get so restless, always needing to do something, rearranging furniture at 3 AM. I know I snap at people more easily during those times, especially if they interrupt me. And I barely sleep a wink, but it doesn't bother me. I just keep going, thinking of what else I can do. It's confusing, these shifts. I can’t quite put my finger on when it started exactly, if it was always like this, or just popped up."

D009-D001_h023.question:
It’s been a rough year, doc. For the past year and a bit, I’ve just felt… empty. Nothing really sparks joy anymore. My usual weekend hikes or even just reading a good book feel like a chore. Getting out of bed is hard, and I feel so heavy, like I’m dragging myself through mud all day. Even simple things at work, like walking to a meeting, exhaust me. It's really started affecting my performance at HR, which is unlike me.

Then, about three months ago, it was like a switch flipped. I suddenly had this surge of energy, like I could conquer anything. Sleep became optional – I’d be up by 4 AM, feeling completely refreshed and ready to go, even on just a few hours. My husband says I was easily agitated during that time, snapping at him for small things, which isn't fair to him. It was a strange contrast, this burst of physical and mental energy. But that intense period has faded now, and I'm back to feeling utterly drained and disinterested. It's confusing.

A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D009-D001_h025.question:
Lately, life has felt like a constant pendulum swing. For the past year and change, I've been in this deep slump. It’s like all the color drained out of my world, and nothing brings me joy anymore—not even teaching piano, which used to be my greatest passion. Some days, I can’t sit still; I’ll pace around the house or wring my hands, but other days, I’m just so drained that even getting out of bed feels like climbing a mountain. It’s really impacted my teaching; I’ve missed lessons, and my students are noticing.

Then, about three months ago, things shifted again. I suddenly had this surge of energy. I was tackling lesson plans, organizing recitals, and even started composing again, sometimes working through the night. Sleep just felt... optional. I didn’t feel tired at all. My husband would say I was a whirlwind, jumping from one project to another, sometimes feeling on top of the world, other times snapping at him for no reason. It was a lot, but I kept thinking, "At least I'm getting things done!" Now, though, the fatigue and the sadness are creeping back in, and I just can't keep up with everything I started. It’s exhausting.
D009-D001_h025.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D009-D001_h025.answer: B & D. Bipolar II Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
